subject: SIG: Airis - deployment model evidence and responsibility matrix
messages:
From: Erin Cho <erin.cho@airishealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@airishealth.com; procurement@airishealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: Clarify hosting modes & evidence for Airis review

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SIG intake we need a concise mapping of Redwood's hosting options (Hosted API, Dedicated/reserved capacity, Private/VPC or on-prem) that clearly states: who controls networking, who has access to customer data at-rest/in-transit, where logs and audit records are stored, and what artifacts you can provide (SOC 2 excerpts, network diagrams, VPC peering docs, onboarding flow for Dedicated).

For scoring we need: a one-page table mapping responsibility (Redwood vs Airis) for data residency, encryption keys, infrastructure access, and a list of evidence we can attach to the SIG. Can you provide that plus any short artifacts by Thursday, June 3? If some items require an NDA or SOW (e.g., on-prem install playbook), call that out.

Also flag any claims that need legal or engineering sign-off (e.g., "no human access to customer data in hosted mode").

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Cho
Head of Security
Airis Healthcare

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Erin Cho <erin.cho@airishealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG: Clarify hosting modes & evidence for Airis review

Hi Erin —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a first draft: a one-sheet matrix that maps Hosted / Dedicated / Private to responsibilities and the evidence we can provide. Attachment: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix_v1.xlsx (see summary below).

High-level notes (from the matrix):
- Hosted API: Redwood manages runtime, key custody optional (we offer managed KMS or customer-managed CMEK for enterprise). Data at-rest in hosted mode is encrypted with AES-256; access to raw customer content is restricted to automated processes for debugging only and requires an internal ticket + audit log. Evidence: SOC2 Type II fragment (attached), hosted network ingress diagram (internal).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Customer-dedicated GPU pool; network isolation via tenant VLANs and firewall profiles; customer can request dedicated VPC peering for private networking. Evidence: dedicated-deployment-checklist.pdf (we'll attach if needed), example VPC peering runbook.
- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customer-managed control plane or full on-prem deploy. Customer owns the network and KMS/HSM. Evidence: on-prem deployment checklist and SOW excerpt (requires legal).

Open questions for Airis that I flagged in the matrix:
1) Desired data residency (region-specific pinned models or additional archival controls).
2) Whether Airis requires customer-managed keys for hosted API or if managed KMS is acceptable.
3) If they need the full SOC2 report (we can provide a redacted copy under NDA) or a few control excerpts.

Attachments in this draft: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix), SOC2_Type2_fragment.pdf (control excerpts).

Karthik/Laura — can you each scan the matrix and confirm the phrasing for the "no human access" claim (I used: "No routine human access to prompt/response content in hosted mode; access paths are audited and limited to remediation workflows"). Also confirm the VPC peering wording: is it accurate to say customers can request a dedicated VPC peering with Dedicated?

I'll push a v1.1 with your edits and return to Airis by EOD Wednesday.

Cheers,
Mina
Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2_Type2_fragment.pdf (pdf extract)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Airis SIG answers - quick clarifications needed

Karthik / Laura —

Quick internal note (threaded off my reply to Airis):
- Karthik: please confirm the exact wording we should use for human access. I used the line below but legal might want it tightened. Suggested authoritative statement: "Redwood does not perform routine human review of customer prompts or completions in hosted mode. Human access to content is limited to engineering remediation workflows and is subject to role-based approvals and immutable audit logs." If OK, I'll include it in v1.1. If not, please propose final text.

- Laura: could you pull a one-page SOC2 excerpt showing CC6/CC7 controls relevant to access logging and encryption? The SIG expects an evidence list and they often accept fragments under NDA. If we can attach a redacted page, note whether legal requires an NDA for the fragment.

Also: network_diagram_airis_v2.png will be a simplified diagram showing Hosted vs Dedicated peering options. I'll generate the initial diagram and would like your read on whether the peering runbook is red-team reviewed.

I'm trying to keep the external language non-technical (Airis asked for a one-page table) but precise enough for their reviewers. Will aim to send v1.1 by Wednesday EOD PT.

Mina

Subject: Re: SIG: Clarify hosting modes & evidence for Airis review (v1.1)

Erin —

Thanks for the patience. Please find updated materials attached: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix_v1.1.xlsx (responsibility matrix with clarifying language) and a SOC2 extract relevant to access logging and encryption (SOC2_Type2_fragment.pdf). Also attached: network_diagram_airis_v2.png (simplified Hosted/Dedicated/Private diagram).

Below is an inline summary you can paste into the SIG: 

Summary table (inline):
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed runtime. Data at-rest encrypted (AES-256). Key options: managed KMS (default) or customer-managed (CMEK) for enterprise (customer controls key lifecycle). Networking: standard internet ingress; customers may request IP allowlists and per-account egress controls. Evidence: SOC2 fragment (attached), hosted architecture diagram (attached). Responsibility: Redwood = runtime, OS patching, physical host security; Airis = application-level access controls and customer key lifecycle if CMEK chosen.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools with tenant-level network isolation. Option: VPC peering for private networking; Redwood supports a documented peering runbook and firewall templates. Evidence: peering runbook (available on request), sample configuration snapshot (attached diagram). Responsibility: Redwood = hardware, VM orchestration, baseline network controls; Airis = VPC routing, firewall rules on customer side, KMS if using customer keys.

- Private/VPC or On-prem: Customer-managed control plane or full on-prem package. Customer retains network, storage, and KMS control; Redwood provides deployment artifacts and optional managed support under SOW. Evidence: deployment checklist and SOW excerpt (requires legal/Sales sign-off). Responsibility: Airis = full infrastructure, key custody, and patching unless otherwise contracted; Redwood = application-level software and optional managed services.

Claims that require additional paperwork or escalation:
- Full SOC2 report: available under NDA.
- On-prem install runbook and SOW: requires a legal-approved SOW and may require additional scoping.

Next steps: if this level of detail is sufficient I'll mark these items in the SIG spreadsheet and attach the three files. If you need a redacted SOC2 PDF under NDA, let me know and I will coordinate with Legal.

Attachments: redwood_sig_deployment_matrix_v1.1.xlsx, SOC2_Type2_fragment.pdf, network_diagram_airis_v2.png

Best,
Mina Haddad
Product Security | Redwood Inference
